solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sacrifice made in the interest of self-esteem?

parts.note: doing something for someone is doing it in their interest
ego is a person's sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: A question of whether some selfless act was really done to make the giver feel good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to give it up or do without it, a synonym of sacrifice; this spelling is an accepted variant.

clue.text: Universal rifle is adjusted for infantyman

indicators.note: adjusting the letters means rearranging them into a new order here

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A soldier's general-purpose gun is tuned up for a foot soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'infantyman', a slip for infantryman.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusilier is a soldier of certain infantry regiments, originally one armed with a light musket.

clue.text: Soldiers parachuting — a bit of a shower

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for soldiers
soldiers parachuting are taking part in an airborne drop, so they are 'in drop'

explanation.surface: Paratroopers floating down like part of a rain shower.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling drop of water is one small part of a passing shower.

clue.text: Cigar-ring drifting over America? Goodness!

indicators.note: letters drifting about have moved out of their original order

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A smoke ring from a cigar floats out across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' shuffles CIGAR to GRACI; in a down clue 'over' puts that and O above US.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Gracious!' and 'Goodness!' are both mild exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: He did noted work on the fountains of Rome

definitions.text: He did noted work on the fountains of Rome

parts.words: He did noted work on the fountains of Rome
parts.note: 'noted' hints at musical notes: the Italian composer wrote the symphonic poem Fountains of Rome

explanation.surface: Someone famous for studying or restoring Rome's fountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted work' sounds like distinguished research but means work written in musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottorino Respighi composed the tone poem Fontane di Roma in 1916.

clue.text: Business logo, perhaps, some deem blemished

indicators.note: some of these words means only part of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: Some people think a company's logo has been spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is one example of a symbolic badge or device, so 'perhaps' marks it as an instance.

clue.text: I snoop around to discover a cause of death

indicators.note: turning the letters around signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A detective nosing about to find why someone died.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxic substances are one way a person can be killed, fitting a detective story.

clue.text: An expulsion order

parts.note: the phrase reads as legal jargon but is just the two-word command telling someone to leave

explanation.surface: An official document ordering someone's removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking 'Leave now!' at somebody is literally an order to expel them, though the phrase as a noun also means an escape route.

clue.text: Wild kids grow up to be adults like these

definitions.text: Wild kids grow up to be adults like these

parts.words: Wild kids grow up to be adults like these
parts.note: kids are young goats, and the wild mountain goats of the Alps have young called kids

explanation.surface: Unruly children turning into grown-ups of a certain type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild kids' suggests unruly children, but these kids are baby wild goats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibex are wild mountain goats, and a young goat is called a kid.

clue.text: It goes round but doesn't join up

definitions.text: It goes round but doesn't join up

parts.words: It goes round but doesn't join up
parts.note: a curve winding round and round a centre never closes into a circle

explanation.surface: Something circling without ever enlisting, like a reluctant recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A coil winding outward around a point never meets its own start, unlike a ring.

clue.text: This bean is used to make a liqueur

indicators.note: the letters are used as raw material and reworked to make something new

explanation.surface: A bean used as an ingredient in distilling some liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: This green anise-flavoured spirit flavoured with wormwood is a strong liqueur.

clue.text: Scots youth I'd lead out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone saying they would lead a young Scot out.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish usage a young lad or boy is commonly called this.

clue.text: Determined to give poor Rose an instrument

indicators.note: poor implies the word Rose is in bad shape and must be reworked

parts.note: a lute is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to give a girl called Rose a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resolute means being firmly set on a course, a synonym of determined.

clue.text: To retire may be the right way out

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right
an egress is an exit or way out

explanation.surface: Advice that quitting work might be the proper exit.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to go back or withdraw, and retire can mean to draw back or retreat.

clue.text: Margaret turned to stone

indicators.note: turned here means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Meg is a short form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: A woman named Margaret was petrified, like a figure in myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone such as a ruby is called a jewel or gem.

clue.text: Big racial issue?

parts.note: issue means outflow: a whole people going out together, as the Israelites left Egypt

explanation.surface: A major question of race relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' reads as a political problem but means an emergence or going out.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass departure of a people, like the biblical flight from Egypt, is a large-scale outpouring of a race.

clue.text: Ready for collection

definitions.meaning: a matching group of things, like a chess or tea service

explanation.surface: Something prepared to be collected.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both prepared to start and a group of things that belong together.

clue.text: Toy revolver

parts.note: reads as a cap gun but means a plaything that revolves, spinning on its point

explanation.surface: A child's toy pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' suggests a gun; it is a toy that spins.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top is a children's plaything that revolves on its tip.

clue.text: Space for some oar movement

indicators.note: movement of the letters means shifting them into a new order

explanation.surface: Rowers need some space to move their oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-room is open water in which a ship has space to manoeuvre.

clue.text: Nasty blow including one in case of injustice

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the mistral is a cold, harsh wind of southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A vicious punch, including one in a case that led to an unjust outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty blow' looks like a punch but is a wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial voided because of an error or unfairness is a legal case that has failed justice.

clue.text: Agonised after explosion in US port

indicators.note: after an explosion the pieces land scattered in a new order

explanation.surface: People in an American harbour city left in anguish after a blast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian city is a major Pacific naval and commercial harbour in the United States.

clue.text: Strongly reminiscent of European river rising fast

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: the Oder is a river of central Europe on the German-Polish border
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Something evoking a European river whose waters climb quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ODER into REDO; 'fast' looks like speed but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: If something strongly suggests or evokes another thing, it is said to be redolent of it.

clue.text: Not a good sailor

parts.note: reads as someone who gets seasick but means a seafarer who is morally bad, a sea robber

explanation.surface: Someone who copes poorly at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a good sailor' suggests seasickness; the sailor is a wicked one.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer who robs ships at sea is a sailor of bad character.

clue.text: Make Andrew go astray

indicators.note: make Andrew do something means rework the name into another word

explanation.surface: Getting a man named Andrew lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray from the path is to roam aimlessly away from it.

clue.text: Two articles supporting embargo for fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit underneath the one they hold up

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade
an is the indefinite article before a vowel
a is the other form of the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces backing a trade ban on some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The long yellow tropical produce is a common fruit.

clue.text: Go over someone's head, being close to exam success

parts.note: by means near or beside
a pass is a successful result in an exam

explanation.surface: A student nearly passing goes over a teacher's head.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass someone is to skip them in the chain of authority and appeal to a superior.

clue.text: Remains in a silent order

parts.note: sh is a command to be quiet

explanation.surface: Something stays put in a monastic order sworn to silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremated human remains are often called ashes, the powder left after burning.

clue.text: Giving publicity to a famous violin piece

definitions.meaning: to air views is to make them public, so broadcasting them
Bach's Air on the G String

explanation.surface: Publicising a well-known piece for violin.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: the famous Bach arrangement is an air played on the G string, read as AIR IN G.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting something gives it publicity, and the punning reading names Bach's well-known Air.

clue.text: Using any sails in storm demonstrates determination

indicators.note: sails caught in a storm are tossed about, mixing the letters

explanation.surface: Sailing through a storm with whatever canvas you have shows grit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'determination' suggests resolve; here it means finding out by examination, as a chemist determines contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical determination is a test establishing what a substance contains, which is a form of examination.

clue.text: I ring the boss before arriving at workplace

indicators.note: the boss comes before the other pieces in order

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob on a surface
a ring is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: An employee phones their manager before getting to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like a manager but is a knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or broadcaster's room for working is called this.

clue.text: Most people want to take part in such society

definitions.text: Most people want to take part in such society

parts.words: Most people want to take part in such society
parts.note: 'take part' means playing a role on stage, as members of an amateur theatre club do

explanation.surface: A remark that most people want to belong to some social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take part' sounds like joining in, but it means taking a part in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur theatre group is called a dramatic society, whose members want acting parts.

clue.text: Did the crew of this ship get two bank holidays?

definitions.text: Did the crew of this ship get two bank holidays?

parts.words: Did the crew of this ship get two bank holidays?
parts.note: the vessel had two banks of oars, so its crew worked two banks

explanation.surface: Wondering if sailors got two public holidays off.
explanation.walkthrough: A bank holiday is a British public holiday; here 'bank' means a tier of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient galley with two tiers of oars on each side was a two-banked warship.

clue.text: It's an indication for drivers, by the way

definitions.text: It's an indication for drivers, by the way

parts.words: It's an indication for drivers, by the way
parts.note: 'by the way' reads as an aside but means placed beside the road

explanation.surface: A casual aside about something motorists should notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like an afterthought but literally means at the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic sign placed beside the road gives motorists directions or warnings.

clue.text: Nearly, but not quite all, the majority

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means one letter is dropped from its end

parts.note: most means the greater part, the majority

explanation.surface: A statement hedged as nearly, though not wholly, the larger share.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean very nearly but falling short of complete.
